info.title: GPU Manager
info.description: Central model runtime of this host: typed model registry, runtime adapters, resource-aware scheduler, one shared queue, model lifecycle, artifacts, watchdogs and telemetry. Service-to-service API (bearer API key per client application). Jobs are submitted in the v1 dialect (operation + params + named inputs) or the generic dialect (model_id + typed inputs[] + parameters); results carry typed outputs.

get.description: Unauthenticated liveness. `blocked` = another process owns the GPUs (GPU Manager is not executing jobs).
Unauthenticated readiness: the engine is ready and every executor thread is alive.
Resource metrics: GPUs, host memory, queue depth by lane, active reservations, job counters.

Service / hardware health, queue (waiting + running jobs, lanes, priority policy, watchdogs, CUDA state), loaded
models with the residency policy and host-memory telemetry, live devices, adapter health, registry summary.

One typed picture for application Settings / System Status screens: service and readiness, host (CPU, RAM,
paging, disks of the model repository / state / training store), every GPU (VRAM used / free / reserved,
utilisation, temperature, power, models placed on it, reservations), queue depth by lane and kind, watchdog,
loaded models (devices, precision, residency, active jobs) and a registry summary. Aggregate data for every client;
the `admin` block (executor threads, per-application jobs, reservation owners, GPU UUIDs, OS detail, this
process' memory) only for the admin scope. Never contains keys, tokens or filesystem paths.

post.description:
Stage an immutable dataset manifest into the host's content-addressed cache from temporary authorized URLs
(https, allow-listed hosts, public addresses only, no redirects). Re-posting the same manifest returns the same stage
and resumes it. Assets already cached (same sha256) are reused without a download. Use a READY stage as a workload
input: {"role": ..., "stage": <id>}.

delete.description: Release the stage (its cached blobs stay for reuse until retention). The owner's objects are never touched.

post.description: Fresh temporary URLs for the still-pending assets (after `awaiting_refresh` or `interrupted`); resumes the download.

get.description: GPUs of this node (live; includes memory used by processes outside GPU Manager). VRAM is never pooled.

Dynamic hardware inventory: every GPU (total / used / free, this service's reservations, utilisation, temperature)
and host memory (available RAM, system commit, this service's private commit / working set, paging).

Operations this node can run (with the installed models that run each, engine options, control-map semantics
and reproducibility notes) plus the generic capability ids registered models expose.

Registry of every model this node knows, with its typed definition (operations, input slots, parameter ranges,
resource / lifecycle profiles, licence). Weights are referenced in place (relative refs; never copied).

post.description: Upload an input (image / audio / file). Re-uploading identical bytes returns the existing artifact (dedup by SHA-256).

Submit an asynchronous inference job; poll GET /v1/jobs/{id} (or /events). v1 dialect: `operation` + `params` +
named `inputs`; generic dialect: `model_id` + typed `inputs[]` + `parameters`. A replay with the same
Idempotency-Key and the same request returns the original job; a different request with that key is 409.

Validate a workload and estimate its resources without queueing it: the adapter's candidate plans, whether it
could be reserved right now (and why not), the current capacity by device.

Run every check a submission would run (configuration against the adapter's schema and rules, runtime environment, inputs and their ownership / hashes, base-model
weights, dataset contract, resource estimate) and report them as `{ok, errors, warnings, checks, dataset, estimate, supported_methods, config_normalized}`. Creates no
job, reserves nothing, starts nothing. The same body as POST /v1/jobs `workload`; a workload that is not `ok` here is refused at submit.

get.description:
Training adapters: framework, tasks, kinds, input formats, config JSON Schema, checkpoint / pause / resume support,
metrics, output contract, hardware features.
Active resource reservations (own ones; every client's for admins) and the current capacity by device.

State transitions of a job (queued, preparing, loading, running, decoding, saving, completed / failed / cancelled)
with messages, plus the live progress. Poll with `after` = the last seq you saw.

post.description:
Training: pause at the next safe boundary (the adapter saves a checkpoint and stops; the reservation is released).
409 `checkpoint_unsupported` when the adapter cannot pause.

Training: start a continuation job from the latest checkpoint of a paused / failed / interrupted job (new job id,
`parent_job_id` set). 409 `checkpoint_unsupported` / `checkpoint_not_found` when it cannot resume.

Queued: cancelled at once. Later states: `cancel_requested` until the adapter stops at its next checkpoint
(denoise step / token / tile). Finished: 409.

get.description:
Read-only job history across all applications, newest first (scope `observe` or `admin`). Summary fields only:
no prompts, parameters, inputs or output content. Page with `next_before`.

get.description:
Resource history sampled every 30 s by the service itself (GPU utilisation and VRAM, host RAM and CPU, queue depth), kept 30 days.
History starts when this version first ran: earlier time is reported as absent, never filled in.

Bounded in-memory tail of this process's WARNING+ log records, newest first (scope `observe`). Secrets are redacted before they enter
the ring; exceptions carry their type and first line only. The ring starts empty at every service start; the full log stays in the file.

Every application identity (`clients.json`) with its rights, key counts, last activity and job statistics. Read-only
(scope `observe`); never any secret or hash.
Managed keys (metadata only; the secret is never retrievable). Legacy `clients.json` keys appear under /v1/admin/applications.

Append-only trail of privileged actions (key create / revoke / rotate, application create, model unload / install, adapter stop,
cancelling another application's job). Never contains a secret.

post.description: Explicitly unload a managed model (frees its VRAM; it reloads on the next job that needs it). 409 while a job runs.

Gracefully stop a model's adapter: a managed worker process exits and its reservation is released; an in-process
adapter is unloaded. 409 while a job of that model runs. The next job starts it again.

Register + install a model for an existing runtime: resolve source / revision, check disk, download into the
central weight store (or adopt a local directory), verify checksums, inspect, write the typed manifest, mark
available. Runs in the background; poll GET /v1/admin/models/installs/{id}. Credentials are never returned.

get.description:
The calling application's own trained models (state, serving status, model id): poll registration without admin keys. The `model_id`
is the only thing a backend stores; it is used as `model` / `model_id` in the normal job API (e.g. speech.transcribe).

delete.description: Explicit deletion of the model's own files. 409 while approved / deployed (retire first) or while another trained model references it.

post.description: Register an EXISTING completed training job (migration / manual): the same code as the automatic hook; idempotent per job.
Re-run the preparation of a failed_preparation model from its preserved original (no retraining).
Record an evaluation result (WER, CER, ...); a `completed` one moves ready_for_testing to evaluation_completed.
Explicit approval: the model becomes `active` (still limited to its owner unless `allowed_clients` widens it). Never automatic.
Unadvertise the model (it disappears from /v1/models and cannot run); its files and provenance stay.

delete.description: Unregister a manifest-installed base model. 409 model_in_use while a registered trained model references it.

JobCreate.title: JobCreate
JobCreate.description:

* v1: `operation` + `params` + `inputs{named slots}` (the model is resolved from `params.engine` / `params.model`);
* generic: `model_id` + `operation` + typed `inputs[]` + `parameters` (+ `output_preferences`, `request_metadata`).
`priority` is an integer (-10..10) or a class: interactive (5) | normal (0) | background (-5).
